summary: Meloxicam is an oxicam NSAID with preferential COX-2 inhibition used once daily for osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Like all NSAIDs it carries boxed warnings for serious cardiovascular thrombotic events and GI bleeding/ulceration/perforation. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration; usual range 7.5-15 mg once daily.
indications: Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (pauciarticular and polyarticular course) in patients >=2 years (oral suspension)

admin: Take once daily, with or without food (with food/milk if dyspepsia)
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Do not combine with other NSAIDs; avoid in the perioperative period of CABG surgery
Ensure adequate hydration, particularly in older or volume-depleted patients
moa: Meloxicam inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (COX), preferentially COX-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis and thereby producing anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic effects. Reduced prostaglandins also account for GI, renal and platelet/cardiovascular adverse effects.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria or allergic reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs
Treatment of perioperative pain in CABG surgery
relative: Heart failure, hypertension, established cardiovascular disease
monitor: Signs of GI bleeding and cardiovascular events

preg: Avoid. Use of NSAIDs at about 20 weeks or later may cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios; use from 30 weeks may cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus - meloxicam is contraindicated in late pregnancy. Avoid in the first/second trimesters unless clearly necessary.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; weigh benefit against potential infant exposure.
renal: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins and can precipitate renal impairment, especially in volume depletion, heart failure or pre-existing renal disease. Avoid in advanced renal disease; in haemodialysis do not exceed 7.5 mg/day.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare severe hepatic reactions occur. Reduce dose in significant hepatic impairment and monitor liver enzymes if symptoms arise.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) and antiplatelets - increased bleeding/GI haemorrhage
Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity, no added benefit
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs + diuretics ('triple whammy') - acute kidney injury and reduced antihypertensive effect
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food/milk can reduce GI upset.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol increases the risk of GI bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum creatinine/potassium and liver enzymes; can cause occult GI blood loss and anaemia.

monitoring: CBC/haemoglobin for occult GI blood loss with prolonged use
Signs of GI bleeding, cardiovascular events and skin reactions
counsel: Take once daily; use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed
Stop and seek urgent care for black/bloody stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, weakness or slurred speech
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory painkillers (including over-the-counter)
Report swelling, breathlessness, unusual weight gain or skin rash/blistering
Tell your doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or on blood thinners
pk: Analgesia within hours; full anti-inflammatory effect over days
~4-5 h (and a second peak ~12-14 h from enterohepatic recycling)
pearls: Boxed warnings: serious cardiovascular thrombotic events and GI bleeding/ulceration/perforation
Contraindicated for perioperative pain in CABG surgery
Long half-life allows convenient once-daily dosing
Watch the 'triple whammy' (NSAID + ACEi/ARB + diuretic) for acute kidney injury
Avoid in pregnancy at >=20-30 weeks (fetal renal/ductus arteriosus effects)
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Symptoms include lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting and epigastric pain, usually reversible with supportive care; serious events include GI bleeding, hypertension, acute kidney injury, respiratory depression and coma. There is no specific antidote; give supportive care, consider activated charcoal within 1-2 h, and cholestyramine may speed elimination. Not removed effectively by dialysis.
